# CI gate
Source: https://docs.nika.sh/sdk/operations/ci

Audit, inspect and rehearse a workflow before protected CI receives provider authority.

<LocalContract />

The pull-request job should prove the file is clean, inspect the authority and
spend shape, then rehearse the graph with the mock provider.

## Admission script

```ts theme={"system"}
import { Nika } from '@supernovae-st/nika-client'

const nika = new Nika()
const file = process.argv[2]
const report = await nika.check(file, {
  model: 'mock/echo',
  nativeStrict: true,
})

if (!report.clean) {
  console.error(report)
  process.exit(2)
}

const run = await nika.run(file, {
  model: 'mock/echo',
  maxCostUsd: 0,
})

for await (const event of nika.events(run)) console.log(event)
const result = await run.done
if (result.status !== 'succeeded') process.exit(result.exitCode ?? 1)
```

## Authority ladder

<div>
  <span>CI ADMISSION · SECRETS ARRIVE LAST</span>
</div>

The review job needs no provider key. Protected execution receives only the
authority its environment and workflow declare.

## Pin and print both versions

```sh theme={"system"}
nika --version
npm ls @supernovae-st/nika-client
```

Keep the engine and SDK release train visible in logs. Do not debug skew from
an implicit global binary.

<Warning>
  Keep this example gated until
  the SDK npm and platform packages are published and their artifacts
  pinned. The matching engine v0.118.7 is already public. `npm view @supernovae-st/nika-client@0.118.7 version` can check
  registry availability; source readiness does not prove a package is pinned
  in CI or that the matching engine artifact is installed.
</Warning>

# Deployment topologies
Source: https://docs.nika.sh/sdk/operations/deployment-topologies

Choose local Nika, the resident firer, authenticated HTTP, an OS bridge or model serve by job.

<ProjectContract />

The word “server” hides several boundaries. Start with who initiates work and
what protocol crosses the process edge.

## Decision table

| Need                                 | Use                          | Status                           | Boundary                                        |
| ------------------------------------ | ---------------------------- | -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| Product code starts a workflow       | local `Nika`                 | Merged SDK source; npm pending   | native process                                  |
| The project clock starts work        | `nika serve` (no `--bind`)   | Live                             | `nika.yaml arm[]` to the resident firer         |
| An application admits jobs over HTTP | `Nika` + `nika serve --bind` | Merged SDK source; public engine | Bearer + OpenAPI · cancellation requests action |
| The host scheduler starts work       | `nika arm --emit`            | Live                             | launchd or systemd to `nika arm fire`           |
| The engine needs local inference     | `nika model serve`           | Live                             | Loopback OpenAI-compatible model API            |

## Request-driven application

<LocalContract />

```ts theme={"system"}
const run = await nika.run('workflows/support.nika.yaml', {
  vars: { ticket: request.id },
})

for await (const event of nika.events(run)) render(event)
const result = await run.done
```

The application owns the user experience and cancellation. The engine owns
workflow admission, execution and the receipt.

## Clock-driven project

```text theme={"system"}
container / bare VM ── nika serve ──────┐
                                         ├── one firer ── run + ledger
managed host ───────── launchd / systemd ┘
```

Both lanes consume the same `arm:` registry. Choose based on who should own
process lifetime and wakeups, not because one lane changes workflow semantics.

## Inference provider

```sh theme={"system"}
nika model serve --model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-GGUF --port 8712
```

This process serves a model on loopback for the engine to call. It does not
accept Nika workflow jobs.

## Loopback HTTP (opt-in)

<RemoteContract />

`nika serve --bind` is not `nika model serve`, and it is not bare `nika serve`.
The pinned OpenAPI exposes cancellation as an action; the runtime's
settlement determines the result. Artifact routes, job listing and
`POST /v1/run` remain absent.

## Architecture view

<div>
  <span>PROCESS TOPOLOGY · NAME THE EDGE</span>
</div>

# OS scheduler bridge
Source: https://docs.nika.sh/sdk/operations/os-schedulers

Emit launchd or systemd user units that fire the project through one engine law.

<ProjectContract />

Use the host scheduler when it already owns wakeups, restarts and process
lifetime. Nika emits the bridge; the engine still owns cadence policy, spend,
locking, firing and proof.

## Preview generated units

```sh theme={"system"}
nika arm --emit launchd
nika arm --emit systemd
```

Without `--write`, the exact unit prints to stdout. Review its working
directory, binary, calendar and environment-file path before installation.

## Write a user-scoped unit

```sh theme={"system"}
nika arm --emit systemd --write \
  --mode user \
  --nika-bin /usr/local/bin/nika \
  --env-file /srv/nika/project.env
```

The live default is user scope. `launchd` writes a macOS user agent. `systemd`
writes a user timer and service pair.

| Option              | Purpose                                               |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `--write`           | Install rather than print                             |
| `--out <dir>`       | Override the generated output directory               |
| `--mode user`       | Keep the unit under the operator account              |
| `--env-file <file>` | Load provider keys without embedding their values     |
| `--nika-bin <path>` | Pin the executable instead of trusting a login `PATH` |

## One firing law

<div>
  <span>OS WAKEUP · ENGINE DECISION</span>
</div>

The generated unit does not reimplement Nika policy. It wakes the engine and
the engine applies the same firer used by `nika serve`.

## Keep secrets out of emitted bytes

The unit carries the path to an environment file, never provider secret
values. `nika.yaml` carries project policy, not credentials. The workflow
declares secret names under its own `secrets:` contract.

## Disarm as a state, not a deletion

```yaml theme={"system"}
nika: my-project

arm:
  - workflow: workflows/nightly-report.nika.yaml
    cadence: "TZ=UTC 0 3 * * *"
    plafond: 0.25
    manqué: sauter
    actif: false
    raison: downstream maintenance
    jusqu_au: 2026-09-01
```

The suspension remains reviewable. `nika arm disarm <label> --write` can remove
generated unit files and teaches the host unload command, but it does not
pretend that removing a unit edited project intent.

# Resident server
Source: https://docs.nika.sh/sdk/operations/resident-server

Operate the stable nika serve firer on a container, VM or bare server.

<SourceContract />

<ProjectContract />

`nika serve` with no `--bind` is the released resident firer. It reads the
`arm:` registry from `nika.yaml`, waits on the wall clock and ends each due
beat at the same firing law as `nika arm fire`. That default process is not
HTTP.

`--bind` + `--workflows` + `--token-file` on the **same verb** opens
authenticated HTTP. The pinned OpenAPI includes jobs, job SSE, cancellation,
trace diagnostics, workflow discovery and schedule read/write. Artifact routes,
job listing and `POST /v1/run` are absent. `--once` and `--dry` cannot bind a
listener.

<Warning>
  Bare `nika serve` is the ARM firer, not HTTP. The HTTP door is opt-in
  (`--bind`). Name the live route contract and its absent routes explicitly.
</Warning>

## Rehearse each operating mode

```sh theme={"system"}
nika serve --dry
nika serve --once
nika serve
```

| Mode     | Behavior                                           |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `--dry`  | Preview calendar-due beats, run and record nothing |
| `--once` | Perform one due sweep, then exit                   |
| no mode  | Remain resident and wait for the next slot         |

`--dry` is intentionally narrower than a real fire. It does not take the beat
lock or apply the complete missed-run, overlap, cost and execution policy.

## Reload without losing the last good registry

<div>
  <span>HOT RELOAD · INVALID EDITS DO NOT REPLACE VALID POLICY</span>
</div>

The server retries a refused edit on a later tick. This keeps a typo visible
without silently replacing valid policy with an empty schedule.

## Read process and beat outcomes separately

Each beat prints one decision line and appends project state. A completed
`--once` sweep exits clean even when an individual workflow failed or paused,
so supervision must read the beat lines and ledgers, not only the outer process
exit.

```text theme={"system"}
resident process
├── stdout line per beat
├── .nika/arm/<label>/history.ndjson
└── .nika/traces/<run>.ndjson
```

## Delivery and shutdown

Ctrl-C and SIGTERM stop the resident loop at its signal boundaries. The ledger
uses durable claims and receipts, which yields at-least-once delivery:

```text theme={"system"}
claim appended ── workflow starts ── receipt appended
       │                  │
       └── crash here ────┴── visible unmatched claim
```

Exactly-once is never promised. Make the workflow's external effects
idempotent when replay would otherwise duplicate harm.

## Opt-in HTTP

```sh theme={"system"}
umask 077
# owner-only bearer file · bytes never enter argv
nika serve --bind 127.0.0.1:18765 \
  --workflows ./workflows \
  --token-file .nika/serve.token
```

Listen line (measured): `nika serve · listening http://127.0.0.1:18765 · GET /health`.

`--workflows <dir>` scopes the served registry (0.118): the listing, the
metadata route and the schedules see only the workflows under that directory,
named from the project root (`flows/quick.nika.yaml`, never `quick`); a
schedule naming a workflow outside it is refused with the teaching. Executed
HTTP workflows use the runtime journal under the project's `.nika/traces/`.
The runtime writes and seals the evidence; `nika trace verify` checks what
was written. A refusal before execution can have no journal, and missing or
incomplete evidence is distinct from a failed run. A cancellation request is
an action: the runtime's eventual settlement, not the HTTP request alone,
determines the result.

`POST /v1/jobs` and `POST /v1/check` take two forms (0.118):
`{"workflow": "<name>"}` for a workflow the served registry lists — the
resident captures the world itself, exactly as a schedule fires — and the
execution snapshot `nika check <file> --json --sdk-snapshot` prints, whose
digests are optional caller-supplied integrity digests (absent, the resident
computes them; present, they must match the bytes). A retry with the same
`Idempotency-Key` finds its job before the registry is read again. The
terminal event (`execution.settled` · `execution.cancelled`) carries the
run's `settlement` whole (`status` · `cause` · `elapsed_ms` · `tasks` ·
`spend` · `error`), the same object `run_settled` flattens; `nika doctor`
says which resident runs (the stores' writer stamp beside the server lease);
`nika explain <code>` teaches every resident code.
The route table lives at `GET /v1/openapi.json`. Full matrix:
[server surfaces](/sdk/operations/server-surfaces).

## Deployment checklist

* Set a stable project `cwd` containing `nika.yaml`.
* Install an explicit `nika` binary path.
* Protect provider keys outside project source.
* Persist `.nika/traces/` and `.nika/arm/` according to policy.
* Capture stdout decision lines.
* Send SIGTERM and allow the active firing boundary to settle.

# Security boundary
Source: https://docs.nika.sh/sdk/operations/security

Preserve argv safety, default-deny permits, secret names, spend ceilings and caller cancellation.

The SDK carries types and transport. The engine remains the policy enforcer.

## Local seam

<LocalContract />

<div>
  <span>PROCESS BOUNDARY · ONE ARGV VALUE</span>
</div>

Local `Nika` transport never wraps workflow paths in a shell string.

## Admit authority before execution

```ts theme={"system"}
const report = await nika.check(file)

if (!report.clean) {
  throw new Error('workflow is not admitted here')
}

authorizeEngineReport(report)

const run = await nika.run(file, {
  maxCostUsd: 0.25,
})
request.signal.addEventListener('abort', () => void nika.cancel(run), { once: true })
const result = await run.done
```

Check these facts explicitly:

* permitted filesystem paths, network hosts, programs and tools;
* model and environment requirements;
* secret names, never values;
* the static cost floor and unbounded flag;
* explicit `cancel(run)` and runtime ceiling.

## Remote seam

<RemoteContract />

Bearer tokens belong in governed environment or workload identity plumbing,
not source. The SDK exposes no logger or webhook verifier; keep application
logging and delivery secrets outside the Nika transport.

## Threat boundaries

| Boundary                                       | Owner       |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| Workflow grammar and permits                   | Engine      |
| Process argv and cancellation verb             | One SDK     |
| HTTP admission timeout and bounded event views | One SDK     |
| Secret storage and identity                    | Deployment  |
| Artifact destination and retention             | Application |

# Server runbook
Source: https://docs.nika.sh/sdk/operations/server-runbook

Boot, supervise, probe, deploy and investigate the stable resident firer.

<ProjectContract />

`nika serve` is a foreground process for one project. A production runbook
should name its room, binary, state volume, signal path and evidence checks.

## Boot gate

Run every probe from the working directory production will use:

```sh theme={"system"}
cd /srv/nika/project
/usr/local/bin/nika --version
/usr/local/bin/nika arm --plain
/usr/local/bin/nika serve --dry --plain
```

This proves binary resolution, project discovery and cadence parsing before a
resident process starts. `serve --dry` is only a calendar preview. It does not
exercise provider credentials or external effects.

## Supervise the foreground process

The minimal systemd service contract is ordinary:

```ini theme={"system"}
[Unit]
Description=Nika resident project firer
After=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=simple
User=nika
Group=nika
WorkingDirectory=/srv/nika/project
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/nika serve --plain
EnvironmentFile=/etc/nika/project.env
Restart=on-failure
KillSignal=SIGTERM

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

Pin `WorkingDirectory` and `ExecStart`. Provider keys stay in the protected
environment file. The project source and `.nika/` volume need only the access
the workflows and evidence policy require.

<Note>
  Units emitted by `nika arm --emit systemd` are per-beat timer bridges. They
  are not the service unit for the resident `nika serve` loop.
</Note>

## Probe the surfaces that exist

`nika serve` does not listen on an HTTP port, so an HTTP health probe would be
a fictional contract.

<div>
  <span>SERVER PROBES · EACH ANSWERS ONE QUESTION</span>
</div>

Treat process liveness and workload success separately. A resident loop can be
healthy while one workflow fails, and a completed `--once` sweep can exit zero
after an individual beat failed or paused.

## Deploy a project change

<Steps>
  <Step title="Stage the exact bytes">
    Put the candidate `nika.yaml` and workflows in the release directory that
    will become the production project room.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Preflight there">
    Run `nika arm --plain` with the pinned binary. A clean report validates the
    arm-ready project and cadence without scheduling work.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Switch deliberately">
    Replace the project release or edit the registry. The resident loop swaps
    only a valid registry and keeps the last good one after a refused edit.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Read the next decision">
    Confirm the process remains live and inspect the next beat line plus its
    sidecar evidence. Hot reload success is not the same as workflow success.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Investigate one surprising beat

Follow one path instead of searching every log at once:

```text theme={"system"}
stdout decision line
        │ label + slot + exit + optional trace
        ▼
.nika/arm/<label>/history.ndjson
        │ claim + receipt or visible unmatched claim
        ▼
.nika/traces/<run>.ndjson
        │
        └── nika trace verify <path>
```

```sh theme={"system"}
nika trace ls
nika trace verify .nika/traces/<run>.ndjson
```

An unmatched claim is evidence of uncertainty after a crash. It is not proof
that the external effect did or did not happen. Keep those effects idempotent
and investigate the external system before replaying.

## Production checklist

* One explicit project `cwd`.
* One pinned binary path and printed version.
* An arm-ready `nika.yaml` for the current released cadence reader.
* Provider secrets outside source and generated units.
* Durable `project/.nika/` storage with chosen retention and access.
* Captured stdout decision lines and stderr diagnostics.
* SIGTERM delivery with enough time for the active firing boundary to settle.
* An incident path from decision to ledger to verified trace.

# Server surfaces
Source: https://docs.nika.sh/sdk/operations/server-surfaces

Separate the resident firer, authenticated nika serve HTTP and local model serving.

Three surfaces sound like servers but accept different clients.

| Surface                       | Job                                        | HTTP workflow API |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ----------------- |
| `nika serve` without `--bind` | Fires the `nika.yaml` project clock        | no                |
| `nika serve --bind`           | Authenticated resident jobs and schedules  | yes               |
| `nika model serve`            | OpenAI-compatible local inference provider | no                |

<ProjectContract />

<RemoteContract />

## Candidate OpenAPI routes

| Method and path                  | Contract                                                                      |
| -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GET /health`                    | unauthenticated health and supported capabilities                             |
| `GET /v1/openapi.json`           | authenticated contract document                                               |
| `POST /v1/check`                 | compact admission acknowledgement or typed workflow refusal                   |
| `POST /v1/jobs`                  | idempotent admission                                                          |
| `GET /v1/jobs/{id}`              | durable job projection                                                        |
| `GET /v1/jobs/{id}/status`       | current status                                                                |
| `GET /v1/jobs/{id}/events`       | SSE event stream                                                              |
| `POST /v1/jobs/{id}/cancel`      | cancellation action; 202 remains pending, 200 returns a completed observation |
| `GET /v1/jobs/{id}/trace/verify` | typed verification diagnostic                                                 |
| `GET /v1/workflows`              | contained names                                                               |
| `GET /v1/workflows/{name}`       | path-free metadata                                                            |
| `GET /v1/schedules/{id}`         | schedule status                                                               |
| `PUT /v1/schedules/{id}`         | CAS-backed schedule apply                                                     |

The contract has no `POST /v1/run`, job-list, artifact, schedule-list,
schedule-delete, trigger or backfill routes. Remote trace verification
currently resolves a typed `unavailable` verdict because the server has no
path-free journal authority; the diagnostic route itself is live.

```sh theme={"system"}
nika serve --bind 127.0.0.1:18765 \
  --workflows ./workflows \
  --token-file .nika/serve.token
```

## Local application path

<LocalContract />

```ts theme={"system"}
import { Nika } from '@supernovae-st/nika-client'

const nika = new Nika({ cwd: process.cwd() })
const run = await nika.run('workflow.nika.yaml')
const result = await run.done
```

This path needs no resident server. These examples target the merged SDK source and public engine v0.118.7.
The matching SDK npm and platform packages remain to be published and pinned.

## Local model path

```sh theme={"system"}
nika model serve --model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-GGUF
```

The engine calls this inference endpoint as a provider. Application code does
not submit workflow jobs to it.

# TypeScript SDK
Source: https://docs.nika.sh/sdk/overview

One Nika facade for local processes and authenticated servers.

<SourceContract />

<ProjectContract />

<LocalContract />

<RemoteContract />

`Nika` is one application seam around the engine. Your product owns the
request, interface and business state. Nika owns parsing, admission,
execution, policy, events, receipts and traces.

```ts theme={"system"}
import { Nika } from '@supernovae-st/nika-client'

const local = new Nika({ cwd: process.cwd() })
const remote = new Nika({
  url: 'https://nika.example.com',
  token: process.env.NIKA_TOKEN!,
})
```

Omit `url` for the native-process transport. Supply `url` and `token` for the
HTTP transport. A contained served name such as `flows/release.nika.yaml`
goes directly to the resident without a local binary or source. An explicit
local path such as `./flows/release.nika.yaml` uses a compatible local engine
to capture immutable bytes before HTTP admission.

## One lifecycle vocabulary

| Intent                | Method                               | Authority        |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ---------------- |
| Audit                 | `check(workflow, options?)`          | Engine           |
| Admit                 | `await run(workflow, options?)`      | Engine or server |
| Observe               | `events(run, options?)`              | Run session      |
| Settle                | `await run.done`                     | Run session      |
| Cancel                | `cancel(run)`                        | Run session      |
| Verify proof          | `traceVerify(receipt, options?)`     | Engine           |
| Recover a durable job | `attachRun(id, options?)`            | HTTP only        |
| Read live status      | `status(run)`                        | HTTP only        |
| Discover workflows    | `listWorkflows()` · `workflow(name)` | HTTP only        |
| Manage one schedule   | `schedule()` · `scheduleStatus()`    | HTTP only        |

`run()` returns after stable admission. It does not return a terminal result.
Events are additive and optional to render; `run.done` is the only terminal
truth for that observation leg, including a pause. A paused durable job may
later resume under engine authority. An admitted workflow failure resolves
as result data. Configuration, compatibility, transport and protocol failures
throw typed SDK errors.

## Documentation graph

<SdkDoors />

## Authority boundary

* The SDK does not parse a second Nika language.
* It does not reconstruct traces or receipts in TypeScript.
* An observer `AbortSignal` does not cancel a run; call `cancel(run)`.
* It does not infer success from an event kind.
* It exposes only the pinned engine's supported routes.

<Card title="Review the merged source" icon="github" href={SDK.sourceCandidate}>
  Inspect the pinned merged SDK source. Publication of its matching npm and
  platform packages remains a separate step.
</Card>


# Arm registry
Source: https://docs.nika.sh/sdk/project/arm-registry

Declare project beats with explicit cadence, spend, missed-run, overlap and suspension policy.

<ProjectContract />

`arm:` is the team registry of workflows the project proposes to fire. The
file proposes. A machine edge disposes. Reading the file never schedules work.

## One beat, complete

```yaml theme={"system"}
nika: my-project

arm:
  - workflow: workflows/daily-brief.nika.yaml
    cadence: "TZ=Europe/Paris 30 7 * * 1-5"
    où: local
    plafond: 0.20
    manqué: rattraper-une-fois
    chevauchement: sauter
    après_saut: prochain-créneau
    par: operations
```

| Key                             | Requirement | Contract                                                  |
| ------------------------------- | ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `workflow`                      | Required    | Repo-relative `*.nika.yaml` path                          |
| `cadence`                       | Required    | Readable schedule, TZ-prefixed cron, or `on-webhook`      |
| `plafond`                       | Required    | Positive per-tick USD ceiling                             |
| `manqué`                        | Required    | `rattraper` · `rattraper-une-fois` · `sauter`             |
| `où`                            | Optional    | `local` by default · `cloud` as the declared remote locus |
| `chevauchement`                 | Optional    | `sauter` by default · `file` for serialized overlap       |
| `après_saut`                    | Optional    | What follows an overlap skip                              |
| `actif` · `raison` · `jusqu_au` | Together    | Auditable suspension state                                |
| `tolérance` · `décalage`        | Optional    | Declared tolerance and deterministic jitter lanes         |
| `par`                           | Optional    | Declared human, not machine authorization                 |

`plafond` and `manqué` have no default. Choosing them implicitly would choose
who pays or whether missed work is duplicated or lost.

## Read before firing

```sh theme={"system"}
nika arm
```

The report names each armed or suspended beat, its next slots, and whether a
sidecar proves a previous fire. It ends by stating that nothing was scheduled.

<div>
  <span>DECLARATION IS NOT PROOF</span>
</div>

## Every door ends at one firer

```text theme={"system"}
nika arm fire <label> ─────┐
launchd / systemd unit ────┼── due window · miss · overlap · ceiling · ledger
nika serve ────────────────┘
```

This convergence matters. Changing how the project wakes up does not change
the firing law.

## Suspend with a reason

```yaml theme={"system"}
nika: my-project

arm:
  - workflow: workflows/daily-brief.nika.yaml
    cadence: "TZ=Europe/Paris 30 7 * * 1-5"
    plafond: 0.20
    manqué: sauter
    actif: false
    raison: maintenance fournisseur
    jusqu_au: 2026-09-01
```

Deleting a row leaves no durable explanation. The suspension triple states
that the beat is inactive, why, and until when.

    Keep the project clock alive without turning it into an HTTP API.
  </Card>

    Emit launchd or systemd user units.

# CWD and monorepos
Source: https://docs.nika.sh/sdk/project/cwd-and-monorepos

Align project discovery, workflow paths, direct-run traces and armed state deliberately.

<ProjectContract />

<LocalContract />

The working directory is not a convenience string. It selects relative
workflow paths, starts project discovery and roots direct-run state.

## Two roots can exist

Project discovery walks from `cwd` toward its ancestors and stops at the first
`nika.yaml`. Direct-run trace storage does not walk upward. It stays under the
process room.

<div>
  <span>ROOT MAP · DISCOVERY WALKS, STORAGE STAYS</span>
</div>

The arm and serve paths enter the discovered project root before they fire.
Their sidecar and triggered-run traces therefore share the project `.nika/`
directory. A direct `nika run` or local `Nika` call writes under its own `cwd`.

## Recommended: align the process room

Set `Nika`'s `cwd` to the project root when one policy boundary and one
evidence well are the goal.

```ts theme={"system"}
// src/runtime/nika.ts
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'
import { Nika } from '@supernovae-st/nika-client'

const projectRoot = fileURLToPath(new URL('../../', import.meta.url))

export const nika = new Nika({ cwd: projectRoot })

const run = await nika.run('workflows/release.nika.yaml')
const result = await run.done
```

That one choice aligns:

* relative workflow arguments;
* upward `nika.yaml` discovery;
* direct-run `.nika/traces/`;
* arm and serve `.nika/arm/` plus triggered-run traces.

## Nested project files are real boundaries

<div>
  <span>MONOREPO · FIRST PROJECT FILE WINS</span>
</div>

A nested `nika.yaml` is useful when a service needs a separate ceiling or
project profile. It is not a path shortcut. Every process below it now sees a
different control plane.

<Warning>
  Review a nested project file like a package boundary. Adding one changes
  policy discovery for every CLI and SDK process started below that directory.
</Warning>

## Probe the production room

Run checks from the exact directory the service manager or container will use:

```sh theme={"system"}
cd /srv/nika/project
nika arm
nika trace ls
nika serve --dry
```

A clean report from the repository root does not prove a nested service uses
the same project file or reads the same trace store.

## Path contract by operation

| Operation          | Project file                          | Workflow argument              | Generated state                                  |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------ |
| Direct `nika run`  | First ancestor from `cwd`             | Relative to `cwd`              | `cwd/.nika/traces/`                              |
| Local `Nika.run()` | First ancestor from constructor `cwd` | Relative to constructor `cwd`  | `cwd/.nika/traces/`                              |
| `nika arm fire`    | First ancestor from process `cwd`     | Relative to discovered project | `project/.nika/arm/` and `project/.nika/traces/` |
| `nika serve`       | First ancestor at startup             | Relative to discovered project | `project/.nika/arm/` and `project/.nika/traces/` |

    Build the root-aligned directory layout.
  </Card>

# nika.yaml project file
Source: https://docs.nika.sh/sdk/project/nika-yaml

Use the released project control plane for policy, armed beats, retention and provenance.

<ProjectContract />

`nika.yaml` governs the project around the SDK. A `*.nika.yaml` file carries
one executable workflow. Keeping those roles separate is the foundation of a
clean application integration.

## Two valid released profiles

Use the arm-ready profile when the project clock starts work:

```yaml theme={"system"}
nika: my-project

ceiling: 0.50

arm:
  - workflow: workflows/daily-brief.nika.yaml
    cadence: "TZ=Europe/Paris 30 7 * * 1-5"
    où: local
    plafond: 0.20
    manqué: rattraper-une-fois
    chevauchement: sauter
```

Use the run-policy profile when application code or an operator starts direct
workflow runs:

```yaml theme={"system"}
nika: my-project

ceiling: 0.50

traces:
  keep: 30d

registry:
  floor: provenanced
```

Both are live. They are separate because the current released cadence reader
does not yet accept the direct-run `traces` and `registry` rungs. The closed
project-shape vocabulary remains . An unknown key refuses with
its line and the accepted set. A present file that silently ignores a typo
would be more dangerous than an absent file, so the parser never drops one.

| Block                  | Project job                                           | Released consumer           |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| `nika: <project-name>` | Project identity (kebab-case name · not a schema tag) | All project readers         |
| `ceiling`              | Default per-run USD ceiling                           | Direct runs and cadence     |
| `arm`                  | Team registry of workflow beats                       | `nika arm` and `nika serve` |
| `traces.keep`          | Project rung for run-journal retention                | Direct run path             |
| `registry.floor`       | Minimum admitted artifact provenance                  | Direct workflow operations  |

## Discover the governing file

The engine walks from the current working directory toward its ancestors and
uses the first `nika.yaml`, like Git finds `.git`.

<div>
  <span>DISCOVERY · FIRST PROJECT ROOT WINS</span>
</div>

<LocalContract />

```ts theme={"system"}
import { Nika } from '@supernovae-st/nika-client'

export const nika = new Nika({
  cwd: '/srv/project',
})

const run = await nika.run('workflows/daily-brief.nika.yaml')
const result = await run.done
```

Prefer a `cwd` at the project root. It keeps workflow paths, project discovery
and `.nika/` state aligned. The [CWD and monorepos](/sdk/project/cwd-and-monorepos)
page documents the split when a nested process room is intentional.

## Found and inspect

```sh theme={"system"}
nika init --project-file
nika arm
```

The init flag lays a commented starter and skips an existing file unless
`--force` is explicit. `nika arm` validates an arm-ready project and cadence
grammar, reports its armed beats and schedules nothing. A direct run consumes
the run-policy profile through the normal project discovery path.

<Warning>
  Do not pass `nika.yaml` to `Nika.run()`. The SDK runs a
  `*.nika.yaml` workflow. The engine discovers `nika.yaml` from `cwd` and
  applies its project policy around that run.
</Warning>

## Continue through the project

<ProjectDoors />


# Project policy ladders
Source: https://docs.nika.sh/sdk/project/policy-ladders

Resolve run ceilings, trace retention and provenance through explicit precedence.

<ProjectContract />

<LocalContract />

The SDK does not replace project policy. It supplies the invocation rung and
the working directory that lets the engine discover the rest.

## Run spend

<div>
  <span>SPEND LADDER · CLOSEST EXPLICIT DECISION WINS</span>
</div>

```ts theme={"system"}
const run = await nika.run('workflows/release.nika.yaml', {
  maxCostUsd: requestBudget,
})
const result = await run.done
```

`maxCostUsd` is invocation-specific. Keep the project default in `nika.yaml`
instead of copying it into every application call.

## Trace retention

```yaml theme={"system"}
nika: my-project

traces:
  keep: 30d
```

The matching `NIKA_TRACE_*` environment knob wins over the project retention
rung, then the engine default applies. This lets an immutable project run
under different operational retention obligations.

## Registry provenance

```yaml theme={"system"}
nika: my-project

registry:
  floor: provenanced
```

The project floor max-composes with the operator policy under `~/.nika`. A
repository can demand stronger provenance. It cannot weaken the machine
owner's floor.

```text theme={"system"}
operator floor ─┐
                ├── maximum ── admitted artifact tier
project floor ──┘
```

## Keep one owner per decision

| Decision               | Owner                                        |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| Project default spend  | `nika.yaml ceiling`                          |
| Request-specific spend | `Nika.run()` call or CLI flag                |
| Scheduled tick spend   | `arm[].plafond`                              |
| Retention by host      | Environment or project `traces.keep`         |
| Artifact provenance    | Maximum of operator and project floors       |
| Workflow authority     | The workflow's own `permits:` and `secrets:` |

<Warning>
  Do not create an application `nikaConfig` object that mirrors every project
  key. That produces a second control plane with no precedence contract.
  Construct `Nika` once with `cwd`; pass only invocation-specific inputs,
  model and ceiling per run. Cancellation is the separate `cancel(run)` verb.
</Warning>

# Project runtime state
Source: https://docs.nika.sh/sdk/project/runtime-state

Persist run traces, firing ledgers, receipts and cadence watermarks deliberately.

<ProjectContract />

Source describes intent. `.nika/` records what the machine did. A production
deployment should choose storage and retention for that distinction before it
runs its first armed beat.

## State map

The unified tree below assumes the recommended setup: direct processes use the
project root as `cwd`.

<div>
  <span>PROJECT STATE · TWO JOURNALS, TWO QUESTIONS</span>
</div>

## Verify a run trace through the SDK

```ts theme={"system"}
const run = await nika.run('workflows/release.nika.yaml')
const result = await run.done

if (!result.receipt) throw new Error('run did not issue a receipt')

const verdict = await nika.traceVerify(result.receipt)

if (!verdict.verified) {
  throw new Error(verdict.output ?? verdict.reason ?? 'verification failed')
}

console.log(verdict.verdict, verdict.trace_id, verdict.exitCode)
```

The SDK returns the engine-issued receipt to the engine for verification. It
does not accept a trace path or inspect the journal in TypeScript. `nika arm`
reads the arming sidecar. They are related evidence, but they are not
interchangeable.

## Persist the clock on servers

A resident server or OS unit needs a durable project state path. If a
container discards `.nika/` on restart, it also discards recent traces and the
watermark used to reason about missed slots.

<Warning>
  The firing contract is at-least-once. A crash after a durable claim and
  before its receipt leaves an unmatched claim in `history.ndjson`. Keep
  external effects idempotent when a repeated fire must be harmless.
</Warning>

## Source-control boundary

```text .gitignore theme={"system"}
.nika/traces/
.nika/arm/
.env
```

Ignoring live state does not mean deleting it on deployment. Mount, back up or
export it according to the workload's evidence and retention policy.

## Evidence lifecycle

```text theme={"system"}
project source ── review ── deploy
                               │
                               ├── arm claim
                               ├── run trace
                               ├── arm receipt
                               └── selected evidence export
```

Export evidence deliberately. Do not turn the entire state directory into a
public application artifact.

# SDK configuration
Source: https://docs.nika.sh/sdk/reference/configuration

Local, remote and per-operation options for the merged One SDK source contract.

<SourceContract />

## Shared bounds

```ts theme={"system"}
interface NikaSharedConfig {
  eventBufferSize?: number      // default 256
  machineBufferBytes?: number   // default 64 KiB
}
```

## Local by default

```ts theme={"system"}
interface NikaLocalConfig extends NikaSharedConfig {
  cwd?: string
  bin?: string
}
```

Engine resolution is explicit `bin`, then `NIKA_BIN`, then the exact optional
platform package. Implicit `PATH` lookup is refused.

## Remote when a URL is present

```ts theme={"system"}
interface NikaRemoteConfig extends NikaSharedConfig {
  url: string
  token: string
  allowInsecureHttp?: boolean
  requestTimeout?: number       // default 30 seconds
  fetch?: typeof globalThis.fetch
  cwd?: string
  bin?: string
}
```

For an explicit local path, `cwd` and `bin` select the compatible local
engine that captures its immutable snapshot. Contained served names go
directly to the resident and do not require either local source or a binary.

## Operation options

```ts theme={"system"}
interface NikaCheckOptions {
  model?: string
  nativeStrict?: boolean
  signal?: AbortSignal
}

interface NikaRunOptions {
  vars?: Record<string, string | number | boolean>
  model?: string
  maxCostUsd?: number
  idempotencyKey?: string
}

interface NikaEventsOptions {
  signal?: AbortSignal
  bufferSize?: number
}

interface NikaAttachRunOptions { lastEventId?: number }
interface NikaTraceVerifyOptions { signal?: AbortSignal }
```

Remote `check` refuses `model` and `nativeStrict`. Remote `run` accepts
`idempotencyKey` but refuses `vars`, `model` and `maxCostUsd` until the HTTP
request envelope can carry them. Signals stop a request or observer; only
`cancel(run)` requests cancellation of admitted work; `run.done` carries the
actual outcome.

    See where each option is consumed.
  </Card>

    Read the exported projections.
  </Card>

# SDK method index
Source: https://docs.nika.sh/sdk/reference/methods

The merged One SDK source contract's lifecycle vocabulary.

<SourceContract />

| Method                           | Returns                            | Local |                 HTTP                |
| -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | :---: | :---------------------------------: |
| `check(workflow, options?)`      | `Promise<NikaCheckResult>`         |  yes  |                 yes                 |
| `run(workflow, options?)`        | `Promise<NikaRun>`                 |  yes  |                 yes                 |
| `events(run, options?)`          | `AsyncIterable<NikaEvent>`         |  yes  |                 yes                 |
| `cancel(run)`                    | `Promise<NikaCancelResult>`        |  yes  |                 yes                 |
| `traceVerify(receipt, options?)` | `Promise<NikaTraceVerifyResult>`   |  yes  | typed unavailable verdict currently |
| `attachRun(id, options?)`        | `Promise<NikaRun>`                 |   no  |                 yes                 |
| `status(run)`                    | `Promise<NikaRunStatus>`           |   no  |                 yes                 |
| `listWorkflows()`                | `Promise<readonly string[]>`       |   no  |                 yes                 |
| `workflow(name)`                 | `Promise<NikaWorkflowMetadata>`    |   no  |                 yes                 |
| `schedule(workflow, options)`    | `Promise<NikaScheduleApplyResult>` |   no  |                 yes                 |
| `scheduleStatus(id)`             | `Promise<NikaScheduleStatus>`      |   no  |                 yes                 |

`run.done` is the result for one observation leg, including a pause.
`check()` returns the engine's local findings report or the resident's typed
served-name acknowledgement/refusal, depending on admission form.
`cancel()` may acknowledge a pending action; it never replaces `run.done`.
Methods that require resident
authority return typed compatibility errors in native mode. `events`,
`cancel`, and `status` accept only a run owned by that client instance.

The facade intentionally has no version, plan, buffered-run, golden-test,
health, webhook, artifact or environment-constructor convenience methods.

    Constructor and operation options.
  </Card>

    Expand the public projections.
  </Card>

# SDK type index
Source: https://docs.nika.sh/sdk/reference/types

Open engine projections, run lifecycle types, proof and error taxonomy.

<SourceContract />

## Run lifecycle

```ts theme={"system"}
interface NikaRun {
  readonly id: NikaRunId
  readonly done: Promise<NikaRunResult>
}

interface NikaRunResult {
  id: NikaRunId
  status: NikaRunStatus
  transport: 'native-process' | 'http'
  exitCode?: number
  outputs?: Record<string, unknown>
  receipt?: NikaReceipt
  error?: NikaMachineError
  execution_id?: NikaExecutionId
  settlement?: NikaSettlement
  [key: string]: unknown
}
```

`NikaRunStatus`, `NikaEvent`, `NikaCheckResult` and engine-owned metadata are
additive. Known words aid completion without closing the vocabulary.

`NikaSettlement` preserves the engine's `status`, `cause`, `elapsed_ms`,
`tasks`, `spend` and `error` when present. Remote replay and attachment read
the stored settlement; a missing runtime settlement remains absent.
`paused` completes the observation represented by `done` while leaving the
durable job resumable. Branded `NikaRunId`, `NikaJobId` and `NikaExecutionId`
keep engine-issued identities distinct and remain assignable to `string`.

## Check and cancellation

`NikaCheckResult` is an open engine projection. A local check carries the
findings report and process `exitCode`. A served-name HTTP check carries
`clean: true` plus `status`, `snapshot_digest`, `root` and `units`, or
`clean: false` with a typed refusal in `error`; it does not invent a local
findings report or exit code.

`NikaCancelResult` describes action acceptance. Its `status` can be
`cancellation_requested` while execution continues toward its own settlement.
Use `run.done` for the actual result, including success racing cancellation.

## Events and proof

```ts theme={"system"}
// Common fields across the open NikaEvent union.
interface NikaEventFields {
  kind?: string
  status?: NikaRunStatus
  sequence?: number
  receipt?: NikaReceipt
  outputs?: Record<string, unknown>
  [key: string]: unknown
}

type NikaReceipt = Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>

interface NikaTraceVerifyResult {
  verified: boolean
  verdict?: 'verified' | 'invalid' | 'unavailable' | (string & {})
  reason?: string
  trace_id?: string
  exitCode?: number
  output?: string
  [key: string]: unknown
}
```

## Errors

```text theme={"system"}
NikaError
├── NikaConfigurationError
├── NikaTransportError
│   └── NikaProtocolError
├── NikaCompatibilityError
├── NikaOperationError
├── NikaEventBufferOverflowError
└── NikaRunOwnershipError

NikaEngineUnavailable
```

`NikaEngineUnavailable` is exported separately by binary resolution. Schedule
types are exported for the exact CAS-backed resident schedule contract; inspect
the merged source declarations for their additive engine-owned fields.

<Card title="Merged source types" icon="github" href={SDK.sourceCandidate}>
  Review the source declarations at the pinned merged SDK commit.

# Outputs and artifacts
Source: https://docs.nika.sh/sdk/remote/artifacts

Use run outputs honestly while artifact HTTP routes remain absent.

<RemoteContract />

The pinned OpenAPI has no artifact list, download or streaming route, and One
SDK exposes no artifact methods. Do not construct URLs or convenience methods
that the server does not advertise.

Engine-owned outputs arrive on events and the terminal result:

```ts theme={"system"}
for await (const event of nika.events(run)) {
  if (event.outputs) preview(event.outputs)
}

const result = await run.done
await persistOutputs(run.id, result.outputs)
```

`outputs` is `Record<string, unknown>` because the workflow defines its own
shape. Validate it at the application boundary before mapping it into business
state.

When a workflow writes files, the engine owns their placement and authority.
Remote retrieval requires a separate application-controlled store until a
future published OpenAPI contract adds artifact routes.

  <Card title="Jobs" icon="list-check" href="/sdk/remote/jobs">
    Keep outputs attached to the run identity.
  </Card>

  </Card>

# Remote client
Source: https://docs.nika.sh/sdk/remote/client

Select authenticated nika serve HTTP with the same Nika facade.

<SourceContract />

<RemoteContract />

```ts theme={"system"}
import { Nika } from '@supernovae-st/nika-client'

const nika = new Nika({
  url: process.env.NIKA_URL!,
  token: process.env.NIKA_TOKEN!,
  requestTimeout: 30_000,
})
```

Supplying `url` selects HTTP. There is no environment-reading constructor:
read and validate deployment configuration in your application.

Contained names such as `release.nika.yaml` or `flows/release.nika.yaml`
select a served workflow. `check()` and `run()` send the name directly to the
resident; no local binary or workflow source is needed. To submit local
source instead, use an explicit path such as `./flows/release.nika.yaml` or
an absolute path. The SDK then resolves a compatible local engine from
`bin`, `NIKA_BIN`, or the exact platform package and captures an immutable
snapshot relative to `cwd`. It never falls back from an unserved name to a
local file.

Plain HTTP is refused unless `allowInsecureHttp: true` is explicit. Reserve
that option for deliberate loopback use. URLs cannot carry credentials,
queries or fragments; bearer tokens must be 32–512 visible ASCII bytes.

```ts theme={"system"}
const loopback = new Nika({
  url: 'http://127.0.0.1:8787',
  token,
  allowInsecureHttp: true,
})
```

`requestTimeout` bounds HTTP admission. `fetch`, `eventBufferSize` and
`machineBufferBytes` are the other transport seams. The SDK does not expose
automatic retry or concurrency policy as constructor options.

## Check a served name

```ts theme={"system"}
const report = await nika.check('flows/release.nika.yaml')
if (!report.clean) {
  console.error(report.error)
} else {
  console.log(report.status, report.snapshot_digest, report.root, report.units)
}
```

A successful served-name check returns `clean: true` with the resident's
compact acknowledgement: `status: "accepted"`, `snapshot_digest`, `root` and `units`.
A missing served name or a workflow admission refusal returns `clean: false`
with the typed resident `error` (`code`, optional `message`). This is not a
local findings report: it has no local process `exitCode` and does not invent
findings. Authentication, transport and protocol failures still throw.

An explicit local-path check retains the local engine's full check report;
when capture succeeds, the resident must acknowledge that exact snapshot
before the SDK returns it. Remote checks reject `model` and `nativeStrict`
overrides because the HTTP request has no envelope for them.

  <Card title="Jobs" icon="list-check" href="/sdk/remote/jobs">
    Admit, recover, observe and cancel durable jobs.
  </Card>

  <Card title="Configuration" icon="sliders" href="/sdk/reference/configuration">
    Read the exact local and remote unions.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>


# Remote jobs
Source: https://docs.nika.sh/sdk/remote/jobs

Admit, persist, recover, observe and cancel resident HTTP jobs.

<RemoteContract />

## Admit and persist identity

```ts theme={"system"}
const run = await nika.run('release.nika.yaml', {
  idempotencyKey: crypto.randomUUID(),
})

await database.runs.insert({ jobId: run.id, lastEventId: 0 })
```

The contained name in this example submits `{"workflow":"release.nika.yaml"}`
to `POST /v1/jobs`; the resident captures its served workflow itself. No local
binary or source is needed. An explicit local path such as
`./release.nika.yaml` instead asks a compatible local engine for a snapshot
and sends those captured bytes.
Remote run options currently accept `idempotencyKey`; `vars`, `model` and
`maxCostUsd` are refused because their request envelopes do not exist.

## Observe and settle

```ts theme={"system"}
for await (const event of nika.events(run)) {
  if (event.sequence !== undefined) {
    await saveCheckpoint(run.id, event.sequence)
  }
}

const result = await run.done
```

## Recover after a process restart

```ts theme={"system"}
const recovered = await nika.attachRun(saved.jobId, {
  lastEventId: saved.lastEventSequence,
})

for await (const event of nika.events(recovered)) {
  if (event.sequence !== undefined) {
    await saveCheckpoint(recovered.id, event.sequence)
  }
}

const result = await recovered.done
```

Persist the job id and the last durably consumed sequence. Reattachment avoids
resubmitting a workflow merely because the Node process restarted.
The engine's settlement remains available on `result.settlement` even when
the cursor already consumed its terminal event. `paused` settles the current
observation leg at a human gate and closes its event view and `done` promise.
The durable job remains resumable by the engine. `attachRun()` resumes
observation; it does not answer a human gate or start the next execution leg.

## Read status or cancel

```ts theme={"system"}
console.log(await nika.status(run))
const cancellation = await nika.cancel(run)
const result = await run.done
```

`cancellation.status` may be `cancellation_requested`: the resident accepted
the action and the runtime is still settling. Await `run.done` for its actual
status, settlement and evidence. A success or failure racing cancellation is
preserved; cancellation grace without a runtime result becomes `interrupted`.
Queued jobs can be cancelled before execution, and an already-settled job
returns its existing result unchanged. The API has no job-list route, so
application indexes remain application-owned.

<CardGroup>
  <Card title="SSE streaming" icon="wave-pulse" href="/sdk/remote/streaming">
    Preserve sequence continuity across observers.
  </Card>

  <Card title="Errors" icon="triangle-exclamation" href="/sdk/runtime/errors">
    Separate run failure from boundary failure.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>


# SSE streaming
Source: https://docs.nika.sh/sdk/remote/streaming

Observe a run through bounded additive event views and durable recovery.

<RemoteContract />

```ts theme={"system"}
for await (const event of nika.events(run, { bufferSize: 64 })) {
  render(event)
  if (event.sequence !== undefined) {
    await persistSequence(run.id, event.sequence)
  }
}
```

`NikaEvent` is open to additive fields and event kinds. Render only what the
application understands, preserve sequence when it is present, and use
`run.done` for terminal truth.

Each subscriber has a bounded queue. If a consumer falls behind, the SDK
throws `NikaEventBufferOverflowError` rather than silently losing evidence.

## Stop one view

```ts theme={"system"}
const controller = new AbortController()

for await (const event of nika.events(run, {
  signal: controller.signal,
})) {
  render(event)
}
```

The signal stops only this subscriber. Call `nika.cancel(run)` to ask the
server to cancel engine work.

## Resume from application state

```ts theme={"system"}
const recovered = await nika.attachRun(jobId, {
  lastEventId: lastCommittedSequence,
})
```

The HTTP adapter uses the persisted cursor for SSE continuity. The application
owns when a sequence is durable.

A `paused` settlement closes the current stream and resolves `run.done` with
that leg's result and evidence. The durable job can later resume under engine
authority; a new attachment can observe that later leg. Replaying or attaching
after the settlement event has already been consumed still reads the full
stored settlement. Stopping a stream or attaching to a job never answers a
human gate.

  <Card title="Jobs" icon="list-check" href="/sdk/remote/jobs">
    Own identity and recovery around the stream.
  </Card>

  <Card title="Runtime events" icon="signal" href="/sdk/runtime/events">
    Build a tolerant presentation reducer.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>


# Application webhooks
Source: https://docs.nika.sh/sdk/remote/webhooks

Own webhook delivery and verification outside the One SDK contract.

<RemoteContract />

The source SDK exposes no webhook verifier, and the server OpenAPI exposes no
webhook registration or delivery routes. Do not call an SDK static verifier or
claim a Nika signature format.

If your application emits webhooks after `run.done`, that is an
application-owned integration:

```ts theme={"system"}
const result = await run.done

await applicationWebhookQueue.enqueue({
  runId: run.id,
  status: result.status,
  outputs: result.outputs,
})
```

Use the receiving platform's published signing library and contract. Store the
Nika run id and receipt alongside delivery state so workflow proof and webhook
delivery remain separate authorities.

    Keep tokens, receipts and application secrets in their own boundaries.
  </Card>

# Workflow registry
Source: https://docs.nika.sh/sdk/remote/workflows

Discover contained resident workflows without exposing source paths.

<RemoteContract />

```ts theme={"system"}
const names = await nika.listWorkflows()

for (const name of names) {
  const metadata = await nika.workflow(name)
  console.log(metadata.workflow)
}
```

`listWorkflows()` returns contained workflow names. `workflow(name)` returns
path-free, engine-owned metadata with an open additive shape.

The source client has no pagination, reload or raw-source methods. The
resident server controls its configured workflow root; applications should
not infer filesystem paths or ask the public API to reveal YAML bytes.

# Errors and results
Source: https://docs.nika.sh/sdk/runtime/errors

Separate dirty reports, admitted workflow results and typed boundary failures.

## Three channels

| Channel                  | Example                                                         | Handling              |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| Resolved report          | `check()` returns `clean: false`                                | show engine findings  |
| Resolved terminal result | `run.done` returns `status: "failed"`                           | branch on result data |
| Rejected promise         | invalid config, incompatible option, transport/protocol failure | catch typed SDK error |

```ts theme={"system"}
const report = await nika.check(file)
if (!report.clean) return { admitted: false, report }

const run = await nika.run(file)
const result = await run.done

if (result.status !== 'succeeded') {
  return { admitted: true, status: result.status, error: result.error }
}
```

## Typed boundary failures

```text theme={"system"}
NikaError
├── NikaConfigurationError
├── NikaTransportError
│   └── NikaProtocolError
├── NikaCompatibilityError
├── NikaOperationError
├── NikaEventBufferOverflowError
└── NikaRunOwnershipError
```

`NikaOperationError` carries schedule operation findings.
`NikaEventBufferOverflowError` refuses silent observer loss.
`NikaRunOwnershipError` prevents one facade from acting on another facade's
run object. `NikaEngineUnavailable` reports local engine resolution failure.

<Warning>
  An HTTP trace verification can resolve with
  `verified: false, verdict: "unavailable"`; that typed engine verdict is not a
  transport 404 and must not be converted into one.
</Warning>

  <Card title="Type index" icon="brackets-curly" href="/sdk/reference/types">
    Scan every public result and error type.
  </Card>

  <Card title="Run lifecycle" icon="circle-play" href="/sdk/local/run-and-cancel">
    Keep observation and settlement separate.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>


# Run events
Source: https://docs.nika.sh/sdk/runtime/events

Consume an additive, bounded event view without replacing terminal truth.

```ts theme={"system"}
type ViewState = { active: Set<string> }

function reduce(state: ViewState, event: NikaEvent) {
  switch (event.kind) {
    case 'task_started':
      state.active.add(String(event.task_id))
      break
    case 'task_completed':
      state.active.delete(String(event.task_id))
      break
    default:
      telemetry.debug('unrendered event', event.kind)
  }
}

const run = await nika.run('workflow.nika.yaml')
for await (const event of nika.events(run)) reduce(view, event)
const result = await run.done
```

Kinds and fields are engine-owned and additive. Unknown events should remain
visible to diagnostics without crashing an older interface. Never infer
completion from the last recognized kind; use `run.done`.

`result.settlement` carries the engine's full settlement, including cause,
elapsed time, task tally, spend and error when present. Remote replay and
attachment preserve it even after the event cursor has passed the settlement.
Unknown evidence stays absent; an interrupted job need not have a runtime
settlement. A paused result ends this observation leg and event view while
leaving the durable job available for a later engine-owned resume.

Each event subscriber has a bounded queue. A slow consumer receives
`NikaEventBufferOverflowError` instead of silent loss. Tune a view with
`bufferSize`, bounded by the client's `eventBufferSize`.

An `AbortSignal` stops only its observer. It does not end engine work. Call
`nika.cancel(run)` when cancellation is intended.

  <Card title="Run and cancel" icon="circle-play" href="/sdk/local/run-and-cancel">
    Open the view and await terminal settlement.
  </Card>

  <Card title="Receipts" icon="link" href="/sdk/runtime/receipts">
    Move from transient presentation to durable proof.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>


# Receipts and verification
Source: https://docs.nika.sh/sdk/runtime/receipts

Persist engine-issued proof and return it unchanged for verification.

A live event view is presentation. An engine-issued receipt identifies the
run and its available evidence; its presence alone does not prove a sealed
journal exists. Refusal before execution, queued cancellation and interrupted
ownership can leave no complete runtime trace.

```ts theme={"system"}
const run = await nika.run('workflow.nika.yaml')
const result = await run.done

if (!result.receipt) throw new Error('run did not issue a receipt')

await auditStore.write({ runId: run.id, receipt: result.receipt })

const verdict = await nika.traceVerify(result.receipt)
if (!verdict.verified) {
  throw new Error(verdict.output ?? verdict.reason ?? 'verification failed')
}
```

`NikaReceipt` is an opaque readonly record. The SDK never constructs it,
extracts a path from it, enriches it by reading a workflow, or implements
cryptography. It asks the authoritative engine to verify the object unchanged.
The runtime writes and seals trace evidence. Verification reads what already
exists; it never creates a journal or seals an incomplete one. Paused results
can carry evidence for the completed observation leg while the durable job
remains resumable.

Local verification can return `verified` or `invalid`. The remote endpoint
currently returns a typed `unavailable` verdict with reason
`trace_journal_unavailable` because it has no path-free journal authority. The
diagnostic route exists; this is not a 404.

CLI trace inspection remains available for operators:

```sh theme={"system"}
nika trace show .nika/traces/<run>.ndjson
nika trace replay .nika/traces/<run>.ndjson
nika trace export .nika/traces/<run>.ndjson
```

Replay reprojects recorded events; it never reruns the workflow.

  <Card title="Test and trace" icon="vial-circle-check" href="/sdk/local/test-and-trace">
    Keep goldens and proof verification distinct.
  </Card>

  <Card title="Run receipts pattern" icon="receipt" href="/patterns/run-receipts">
    Carry receipts through application boundaries.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>


# Project setup
Source: https://docs.nika.sh/sdk/start/project-setup

Give workflows, binary resolution, traces and application code an explicit boundary.

<LocalContract />

<ProjectContract />

The SDK should make the project boundary visible, not dissolve it into
application objects. The root `nika.yaml` is the control plane. Each
`*.nika.yaml` file is executable workflow intent.

## Recommended layout

<div>
  <span>PROJECT TREE · CONTROL PLANE + INTENT + PROOF</span>
</div>

* `nika.yaml` governs project-wide spend and the released reader profile this
  project uses.
* `workflows/` is reviewed as intent.
* `src/nika.ts` owns binary resolution and the working directory, not a
  second copy of project policy.
* `.nika/` is runtime state. Ignore it in source control and mount it
  deliberately on a server.

## Found the project

```sh theme={"system"}
nika init --project-file --recipe starter
nika arm
```

`--project-file` is the scripted door to the starter. It skips an existing
file unless `--force` is explicit. Bare `nika arm` reads and validates the
project and cadence grammar, reports what is armed, and schedules nothing.

The starter is optional and comments every governing example. Start with the
common rung that the released reader accepts — the same identity
`nika init --project-file` writes:

```yaml theme={"system"}
nika: my-project

ceiling: 0.50
```

Add `arm:` when time or an event should start a workflow. Add `traces:` or
`registry:` for direct-run policy. The current cadence path does not compose
those two profiles yet, so the dedicated [project file](/sdk/project/nika-yaml)
and [arm registry](/sdk/project/arm-registry) pages show valid copy-paste forms
for each lane.

## Create one client

```ts theme={"system"}
// src/nika.ts
import { Nika } from '@supernovae-st/nika-client'

export const nika = new Nika({
  bin: process.env.APP_NIKA_BIN,
  cwd: new URL('..', import.meta.url).pathname,
})
```

Binary resolution follows one ladder:

1. `bin` passed to the constructor
2. `NIKA_BIN`
3. exact optional platform package

Use an explicit application variable for packaged services. Implicit `PATH`
lookup is refused. `cwd` anchors relative workflow paths,
project-file discovery and the `.nika/` state directory.

## Probe at startup

```ts theme={"system"}
try {
  const report = await nika.check('workflows/daily-brief.nika.yaml', {
    nativeStrict: true,
  })
  console.info('nika engine ready', report.clean)
} catch (error) {
  console.error('cannot start workflow runtime', error)
  process.exit(3)
}
```

A missing binary is an environment failure. A dirty workflow is different:
`check()` resolves to a report so the caller can show every finding.

## Keep receipts governed

```text .gitignore theme={"system"}
.nika/traces/
.nika/arm/
.env
```

Traces may carry run metadata and outputs. Arm state carries firing claims,
receipts and cadence watermarks. If a deployment retains them, choose the
volume, retention window and access policy explicitly.

# TypeScript quickstart
Source: https://docs.nika.sh/sdk/start/quickstart

Audit a real workflow and complete one typed run through the One SDK lifecycle.

<SourceContract />

<LocalContract />

<ProjectContract />

The default client is local. It needs no server or token, but it does need
Node.js 22 or newer and a compatible Nika engine.

## 1. Check package availability

```sh theme={"system"}
nika --version
npm view @supernovae-st/nika-client@0.118.7 version
```

The SDK source is merged and the matching engine v0.118.7 is public.
The SDK npm package at this version remains unpublished. The remaining
examples require that exact SDK and engine. Wait for its package and platform
artifacts before installing from the registry. After publication, verify the exact
version rather than the moving npm `latest` tag:

```sh theme={"system"}
npm install @supernovae-st/nika-client@0.118.7
node -p "require('@supernovae-st/nika-client/package.json').version"
```

The second command proves the dependency installed in this project. A version
query alone does not prove that the engine or optional platform package is
the matching released artifact.

## 2. Create a project and workflow

```sh theme={"system"}
nika init --project-file
mkdir -p workflows
nika new 01-hello workflows/hello.nika.yaml
```

Keep the generated `.nika.yaml` workflow in your application, for example as
`workflows/hello.nika.yaml`.

`nika.yaml` is the project control plane; `workflows/hello.nika.yaml` is the
executable workflow. Pass only the latter to `check()` and `run()`.

## 3. Check, admit, observe, settle

```ts theme={"system"}
import { Nika } from '@supernovae-st/nika-client'

const nika = new Nika({ cwd: process.cwd() })
const file = 'workflows/hello.nika.yaml'
const report = await nika.check(file, { nativeStrict: true })

if (!report.clean) {
  console.error(report)
  process.exit(2)
}

const run = await nika.run(file, {
  model: 'mock/echo',
  maxCostUsd: 0,
})

const watching = (async () => {
  for await (const event of nika.events(run)) {
    console.log(event.kind, event.status)
  }
})()

const result = await run.done
await watching

if (result.status !== 'succeeded') process.exit(result.exitCode ?? 1)
console.log(result.settlement, result.outputs, result.receipt)
```

`run()` resolves after stable admission. `nika.events(run)` is the live,
additive journal view. `run.done` is the only terminal result; an admitted
workflow failure resolves as `status: "failed"` instead of throwing.

## 4. Verify engine-issued proof

```ts theme={"system"}
if (!result.receipt) throw new Error('run did not issue a receipt')

const proof = await nika.traceVerify(result.receipt)
if (!proof.verified) {
  throw new Error(proof.output ?? proof.reason ?? 'trace verification failed')
}
```

Pass the receipt object back unchanged. The SDK transports proof; the engine
owns verification. Verification reads existing evidence; it does not create
or seal a journal. A receipt or job identity alone does not guarantee that a
trace is available.
